what_it_is: Bite-sized fried boneless chicken thigh in the style of South Indian Chicken 65, served on and with thick fried corn chips. It is a design in development and has not been cooked.
why_it_exists: The chip becomes the plate, so chicken and chip are built to be eaten together. It is a shareable, hands-on opener that shows the Indo-Mex idea immediately.
indian_component: Chicken 65 with a yogurt, ginger, garlic and lemon marinade, curry leaf and green chile. It is associated with Chennai, but its origin is contested.
mexican_component: Fried nixtamal corn totopos as the base, with lime, onion and crema. The thick chip is NASHA's own design choice, not a Mexican standard.
fusion_logic: The chicken and chip are eaten as one bite, with crema as an optional cooler in place of raita. Three constructions (integrated, ring, composed board) are planned for comparison.
portion_intent: Shareable board or plate; exact amounts are still to be set in testing.
plating_intent: Board or plate, with crema on the side or worked in depending on the construction under test.
identity_critical_ingredients: Boneless chicken thigh, rice flour and cornflour coating, curry leaf, green chile, fried corn tortilla wedges, lime.
cultural_risk: Medium. The Chicken 65 origin and the Hyderabad or Andhra lineage are unconfirmed, so no single origin story should be told, and an advisor should review.

what_it_is: A small corn-tortilla taco filled with charred, spiced paneer, green salsa, raw onion, cilantro and lime. It has not been cooked.
why_it_exists: It gives vegetarian guests a hero dish rather than a side, and shows that tikka char and taco freshness fit naturally together.
indian_component: Paneer tikka: a thick hung-curd marinade, char and soft paneer. It comes from the North Indian and Punjabi restaurant tradition, and no inventor is documented.
mexican_component: Corn tortilla with salsa verde, onion, cilantro and lime; the taco form is Mexican-inspired. Optional charred pineapple is an echo of al pastor but is never called that.
fusion_logic: Tandoor-style char on a taco, with salsa and lime doing the job that raita and chutney do beside tikka.
plating_intent: Two tacos on a plate with salsa on the side.
identity_critical_ingredients: Paneer, hung-curd marinade with ginger, garlic, chile, kasuri methi and chaat masala, corn tortilla, salsa verde, onion, cilantro, lime.
cultural_risk: Medium. Pineapple is flagged as uncertain and needs advisor input, and the taco form and tikka are both borrowed, so both cultures should be credited plainly.

what_it_is: A slow braise of bone-in goat in a guajillo and ancho chile adobo, served as tacos with a small cup of consomme. It has not been cooked and is a long-lead item.
why_it_exists: Birria de chivo is commonly made with goat in Jalisco (web sources, T1; a Mexican advisor is to confirm), and and it lets NASHA make a rich, deep centrepiece that clearly reads as goat.
indian_component: Technique only: dum-style sealed-pot braising, whole-spice toasting and bhuna-style frying of the adobo paste. Yogurt-papaya and curry-leaf ideas are tested against a plain adobo, not assumed.
mexican_component: Goat, chile adobo, consomme, corn tortillas, onion, cilantro, lime and salsa. These are historically supported from web sources, with a Mexican advisor still to confirm.
fusion_logic: The Mexican dish stays whole, and the Indian layer is included only where tasting shows it adds depth. The dipped and griddled taco form is a modern adaptation.
portion_intent: Taco or tacos with consomme in a small cup; no cheese by default.
plating_intent: Tacos on a plate and consomme in a small clay or steel cup, with bones and fibre kept visible.
identity_critical_ingredients: Bone-in goat, guajillo and ancho adobo, goat, chicken or vegetable stock only, corn tortillas, onion, cilantro, lime.
cultural_risk: Higher. Birria is a living Mexican regional dish, so Mexican advisor review is needed, and the sealed-pot link to India is a parallel rather than a shared origin.

what_it_is: A corn-tortilla taco with roasted cauliflower florets, a tamarind and guajillo glaze, lime slaw, salsa, pickled onion and cilantro. It has not been cooked.
why_it_exists: It is a vegetarian taco meant to stand on its own, with the cauliflower recognisable and not hidden under batter.
indian_component: Inspired by Gobi 65 and tandoori gobi. Gobi Manchurian is Indo-Chinese and is only named if actually used.
mexican_component: Corn tortilla, lime-cabbage slaw, salsa, pickled onion and cilantro. No traditional Mexican cauliflower taco is claimed.
fusion_logic: Roast-first cauliflower with a late tamarind and guajillo glaze, so slaw and pickle add the acid and crunch. A batter-fried version is a comparison, and fry versus roast is still undecided.
portion_intent: Two tacos, three to four florets per taco.
plating_intent: Two tacos, with salsa on the side and slaw and glaze added at the last moment.
identity_critical_ingredients: Cauliflower florets, tamarind and guajillo glaze, lime slaw, corn tortilla, pickled onion, cilantro.
cultural_risk: Lower to medium. The glaze is an original house idea with no claimed precedent, and the dish should be called modern fusion and not traditional.

what_it_is: A griddled quesadilla filled with reduced butter chicken, charred chicken, melting cheese and roasted poblano strips. It has not been cooked.
why_it_exists: It takes one of the best-known Indian comfort dishes and puts it in a handheld, shareable Mexican form.
indian_component: Murgh makhani: a tomato, butter and cream gravy with kasuri methi and tandoori-style charred chicken. Its origin is contested in court, so we do not pick a side.
mexican_component: Quesadilla con rajas: roasted poblano strips and Oaxaca-style cheese, griddled on a comal.
fusion_logic: The makhani is reduced until clingy so it stays inside, and poblano smoke and acid balance the richness. A dip is optional and served separately.
portion_intent: One large folded tortilla, cut into wedges.
plating_intent: Wedges cut to show the cross-section, with the dip in a cup.
identity_critical_ingredients: Chicken thigh, reduced makhani, roasted poblano rajas, Oaxaca-style cheese, tortilla, kasuri methi.
cultural_risk: Medium. The dish's origin is disputed, so we should tell no single origin story, and the quesadilla con rajas is borrowed from Mexican home cooking and should be credited.
